audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo del 2,24%, Shanghai in rialzo dell'1,07%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 è in calo dello 0,79%, il VIX è in calo del 5,48%, il Dollar Index è in calo dello 0,38%. L'oro è in calo dello 0,71%, il Brent è in rialzo dell'1,33%. Il rendimento del Treasury USA a 10 anni è in rialzo dello 0,88%, il BTP a 10 anni è pressoché invariato. In sintesi, i mercati mostrano una propensione al risk‑off, con il dollaro più debole, le azioni statunitensi in ribasso e la volatilità in diminuzione.

In Ucraina, il governo ha deciso di acquistare componenti per droni cinesi con fondi dell'UE, segnale di maggiore cooperazione militare. Allo stesso tempo, il vertice della NATO si avvicina, con dibattiti sulla coesione dell'alleanza e possibili tensioni sotto la superficie. Questi sviluppi mantengono alta l'attenzione geopolitica e possono influenzare i prezzi dell'energia e dei materie prime.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i sessantaquattromiladuecentonovantasette dollari, in rialzo dello zero virgola tre percento. L'afflusso netto giornaliero degli ETF è di ventuno virgola uno milioni di dollari. L'inflazione più fresca del dato CPI rafforza le aspettative di tagli dei tassi, ma i trader rimangono cauti. Ethereum avanza a milleduecentosessantacinque dollari, guadagnando quattro virgola sei tre percento, sostenuto da flussi di capitale verso gli asset a rendimento più elevato. Solana sale a settantasette dollari e cinquantaquattro centesimi, con un incremento di tre virgola due sei percento, spinto da interesse crescente nei protocolli DeFi. Il sentiment di mercato è segnato da un indice Fear & Greed di venticinque, classificato come paura estrema. Questo suggerisce cautela tra gli investitori, con una propensione a ridurre l'esposizione rischiosa.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

The Nikkei closed up 2.24%, Shanghai up 1.07%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets.

The S&P 500 is down 0.79%, the VIX down 5.48%, the Dollar Index down 0.38%. Gold is down 0.71%, Brent up 1.33%. The 10‑year U.S. Treasury yield is up 0.88%, the 10‑year BTP is essentially flat. In summary, markets show a risk‑off bias, with a weaker dollar, U.S. equities slipping and volatility easing.

In Ukraine, the government has decided to purchase Chinese drone components with EU funds, signaling deeper military cooperation. At the same time, the NATO summit approaches, with debates on alliance cohesion and possible underlying tensions. These developments keep geopolitical attention high and could affect energy and commodity prices.

No major macro data scheduled for release today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above $64,297, up 0.3%. Daily net ETF inflow stands at $21.1 million. The latest CPI inflation data bolsters rate‑cut expectations, but traders stay cautious. Ethereum advances to $2,265, gaining 4.63%, supported by capital flows toward higher‑yield assets. Solana climbs to $77.54, up 3.26%, driven by growing interest in DeFi protocols. Market sentiment is marked by a Fear & Greed index of 25, classified as extreme fear. This suggests caution among investors, with a tilt toward reducing risky exposure.

No macro data on the agenda today. For a deeper dive into today's topics, visit our platform for the full articles in the Featured Stories section. Thank you for listening and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The AI investment race
articles.snippet: by Phurichai Rungcharoenkitkul The AI build-out ranks among the largest technology-driven investment booms in US history. Its scale, reliance on debt and circular equity ties raise questions about the boom's sustainability and financial stability. We study a dynamic contest in which firms competing for a few dominant positions over-commit resources. The over-investment leaves the sector exposed to revenue disappointment that could turn boom into bust. The larger the boom, the deeper the eventual bust. The race to commit early through debt and circular financing also makes a bust more likely. Calibrated to balance sheet and deal data, the model points to over-investment of around 1.5 times the efficient level, rising to around three times where demand is less elastic. articles.title: AI disruption in private credit: exposure to software firms in BDCs
articles.snippet: by Fernando Avalos, Giulio Cornelli, Egemen Eren Business development companies (BDCs) have lent around $115 billion to software firms, which represents about a fifth of all their lending and over 80% of their fast-growing technology portfolios. Borrowers' revenue uncertainty posed by generative artificial intelligence has not affected these loans yet, and neither BDCs nor their equity investors have priced software exposure differently. Recently, credit spreads have narrowed, reducing the buffers to absorb losses, and a few large BDCs are exposed to a shared pool of borrowers, though low leverage and secured lending may limit spillovers.
